nodes.summary: The finite-population average treatment effect `(1/N) ∑ᵢ (y₁ᵢ - y₀ᵢ)`.
nodes.title: Finite-population average treatment effect

nodes.summary: If treatment assignment is strongly ignorable given the covariate `X`, it is strongly ignorable given any balancing score `b(X)`.
nodes.title: Rosenbaum & Rubin (1983), Theorem 3

nodes.summary: Strong ignorability is inherited by measurable functions of the potential outcomes.
nodes.title: Strong ignorability passes to functions of the potential outcomes

nodes.summary: A function `b(X)` of the covariate is a balancing score (`T ⊥ X | b(X)`) if and only if it is finer than the propensity score: covariate values of positive probability with the same `b` have the same propensity. (Theorem 1 is the case `b = e`.)
nodes.title: Rosenbaum & Rubin (1983), Theorem 2

nodes.summary: The propensity score `e(X) = P(T | X)` is a balancing score: given `e(X)`, the treatment is conditionally independent of the covariate `X`.
nodes.title: Rosenbaum & Rubin (1983), Theorem 1

nodes.summary: The event `T` is conditionally independent of `V` given `W`, stated through the values of `W`: `P(T, V ∈ B, W = w) P(W = w) = P(T, W = w) P(V ∈ B, W = w)` for all measurable `B` and all `w`. For a `W` with countably many values this is the conditional independence of the indicator of `T` and `V` given `W`.
nodes.title: Conditional independence given a discrete variable

nodes.summary: The difference in means for the treated set `S`: the mean of the treated outcomes `y₁` over `S` minus the mean of the control outcomes `y₀` over the complement.
nodes.title: Difference-in-means estimator

nodes.summary: Under strong ignorability of `T` given a finitely-valued `X` for the pair `(Y₀, Y₁)`, `E[1_T Y / e(X) - 1_{Tᶜ} Y / (1 - e(X))] = E[Y₁ - Y₀]`.
nodes.title: Identification of the average treatment effect by inverse probability weighting

nodes.summary: Inverse probability weighting, control arm: under strong ignorability of `T` given `X` for `Y₀`, `E[1_{Tᶜ} Y / (1 - e(X))] = E[Y₀]`.
nodes.title: Inverse probability weighting

nodes.summary: Let the covariate information be a sub-σ-algebra `m` (for example the one generated by `X`), and `e = P(T | m)` the propensity score. If `Y₁` is integrable, the treatment is mean-ignorable for `Y₁`, `E[1_T Y₁ | m] = e E[Y₁ | m]` (implied by `Y₁ ⊥ T | m`), and overlap holds in the strong form `e ≥ ε > 0`, then `E[1_T Y / e] = E[Y₁]` for the observed outcome `Y`.
nodes.title: Inverse probability weighting with a general covariate

nodes.summary: Inverse probability weighting (Horvitz & Thompson 1952; Rosenbaum 1987): under strong ignorability of `T` given a finitely-valued covariate `X` for the treated potential outcome `Y₁`, `E[1_T Y / e(X)] = E[Y₁]`, where `Y` is the observed outcome.
nodes.title: Inverse probability weighting

nodes.summary: Neyman's variance estimator `s₁² / n₁ + s₀² / n₀` for the treated set `S`.
nodes.title: Neyman's variance estimator

nodes.summary: The observed outcome: `Y₁` on the treated event `T`, `Y₀` off it (consistency).
nodes.title: Observed outcome from potential outcomes

nodes.summary: The mean of a finite population of `N = Fintype.card ι` units, `(1/N) ∑ᵢ yᵢ`.
nodes.title: Mean of a finite population

nodes.summary: The variance of a finite population with divisor `N - 1`, `S² = ∑ᵢ (yᵢ - ȳ)² / (N - 1)`; meaningful for `N ≥ 2`.
nodes.title: Variance of a finite population

nodes.summary: The propensity score is calibrated: among units with score `c` (an event of positive probability), the proportion treated is `c`.
nodes.title: Calibration of the propensity score

nodes.summary: The propensity of the event `T` given `W = w`, `P(T ∩ {W = w}) / P(W = w)`. Meaningful for `P(W = w) > 0`; it is `0` (a junk value) when `P(W = w) = 0`.
nodes.title: Propensity score

nodes.summary: Under complete randomization with `n₁ ≥ 1` treated and `n₀ ≥ 1` control units, the difference in means is unbiased for the finite-population average treatment effect.
nodes.title: Neyman (1923)

nodes.summary: The expectation of Neyman's variance estimator under complete randomization with at least two treated and two control units is `S₁²/n₁ + S₀²/n₀` (the sample variances are unbiased for the population variances under sampling without replacement).
nodes.title: Expectation of Neyman's variance estimator under complete randomization

nodes.summary: The variance of the difference in means under complete randomization is `S₁²/n₁ + S₀²/n₀ - S_τ²/N`, where `S_τ²` is the population variance of the unit-level effects `τᵢ = y₁ᵢ - y₀ᵢ` and `n₀ = N - n₁`.
nodes.title: Neyman (1923)

nodes.summary: The expectation of a statistic `f` of the treated set under complete randomization: the treated set is uniform among the `(N choose n₁)` sets of `n₁` units (`n₁ ≤ N`; for `n₁ > N` there is no such set and the value is `0`).
nodes.title: Expectation of a statistic under complete randomization

nodes.summary: Its expectation under complete randomization is at least the variance of the difference in means, with equality exactly when the treatment effect `y₁ᵢ - y₀ᵢ` is the same for all units.
nodes.title: Neyman's variance estimator is conservative

nodes.summary: The mean of `y` over a set of units `S`, `(1/|S|) ∑_{i ∈ S} yᵢ` (the junk value `0` for `S = ∅`).
nodes.title: Sample mean over a set of units

nodes.summary: The sample variance of `y` over `S` with divisor `|S| - 1`; meaningful for `|S| ≥ 2` (for `|S| ≤ 1` it is the junk value `0`).
nodes.title: Sample variance over a set of units

nodes.summary: Rosenbaum & Rubin (1983), Theorem 3 for the propensity score: if treatment assignment is strongly ignorable given the covariate `X`, it is strongly ignorable given `e(X)`.
nodes.title: Rosenbaum & Rubin (1983), Theorem 3

nodes.summary: Strong ignorability of the treatment `T` given `W` for the potential outcomes `V` (Rosenbaum & Rubin 1983): `T ⊥ V | W` and overlap, `0 < P(T | W = w) < 1` for every value `w` of positive probability.
nodes.title: Strong ignorability

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
